newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ebner says Swiss Re has Winterthur stake.
newsitem.headline: Ebner says Swiss Re has Winterthur stake.

text.p: Swiss financier Martin Ebner, who runs the BK Group of investment funds, said a letter he purported came from Winterthur Insurance showed Swiss Reinsurance held at least five percent of Winterthur.
Ebner showed a copy of the letter to reporters late on Thursday and no comment from Winterthur or Swiss Re was immediately available.
Stamped as received by the BK Group on July 4, the document appeared to be a response to a request for registration of Winterthur shares recently bought by BK Vision, one of Ebner's funds.

The letter signed by Dr Juerg Spiller acknowledged BK Vision's request but added that Winterthur statutes did not grant more than five percent of voting rights to any single shareholder or allied shareholders.

"We wish to inform you as a matter of good form that 4,117 shares can only be registered without voting rights based on the aforementioned rules, since Swiss Reinsurance Group has already reached the five percent limit," the letter said.
Ebner said he did not understand how Winterthur had brought BK Vision into connection with Swiss Re.
Winterthur's annual financial report for 1996 said there were no shareholders with five percent or more as of the end of last year.
Ebner said he believed the letter might indicate that several big buyers were out for Winterthur shares, whose sharp rise this week has puzzled traders and analysts.
"It seems some companies may be trying to build up positions before something happens with Winterthur," he said without going into more specifics.
Winterthur registered shares rose over 7.5 percent from Monday through Thursday's close at 1,438 Swiss francs and spiked to a brief all-time high of 1,525 francs.
